get.summary: Long-poll an operation's events.
get.description:
Auth: `cookie|bearer`. Waits up to `waitMs` (clamped to 30000) for an event with `sequence > after`, polling
every 250 ms and returning at most 200 events. A timeout is a `200` with an empty `events` array and
`nextAfter = after`; on a hit the freshly re-read operation is returned alongside. `Last-Event-ID` is not
read — resume by passing the previous `nextAfter` as `after`.

post.summary: Stripe events.
post.description:
Auth: the `Stripe-Signature` header over the raw body. Records the event and enqueues `ProcessStripeEvent`
in one transaction; a duplicate event id is acknowledged without enqueuing (§5.6).

parameters.name: Stripe-Signature
parameters.description: Stripe's `t=…,v1=…` signature over the raw body

requestBody.description: The raw Stripe event body (signature is checked over these bytes)

200.description: Recorded, and enqueued unless the event id was already stored

400.description: `invalid_request`: bad or missing signature; the body is logged as a SHA-256 hash only

expiresAt.description: Null only for legacy keys without an expiry. New keys always expire.

slug.description: personal account slugs are always `u-<first 12 hex of the user id>` (§3.3.3)

knownHosts.description: Pinned OpenSSH `known_hosts` entries for private Git and remote SSH hosts.

mcp.description: Native MCP definitions. Secrets should use `${VARIABLE}` references to encrypted environment.

model.description: Router model ID, e.g. `openai/gpt-5-nano`. None uses the live router default.

permissions.description: Native permission action or tool -> action/pattern map.

Amount.description:
One amount in every unit a client may want to display.
Example: `{"nanos":"10000000000","credits":"10000.000000","usd":"10.000000000"}`

AttachResponse.description:
`{"gatewayUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:18081/ws/0192…","ticket":"hct_…","expiresAt":"…","cliCommand":"haarness attach http://127.0.0.1:18081/ws/0192… --token hct_…","desktopUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:18081","generationId":"…"}`

`cliCommand` carries the ticket in argv for copy-paste convenience (tickets are short-lived and revocable;
`haarness attach` also reads `HAARNESS_SERVER_TOKEN`, which docs/API.md recommends for scripts). A ticket is
bound to `generationId`: after a restart the gateway answers `400 remote_project "workspace restarted; re-attach"`
and the client calls attach again (tickets are NOT revoked at stop).

upstream errors are passed through byte-for-byte.)

Example: `{"code":"insufficient_credits","message":"included AI credits exhausted and overage is not enabled","requestId":"01J8…","retryable":false,"details":{"unit":"nanos","requested":"72000","available":"0"}}`
